From £6.99 to £299.99. Shop by price from the homepage to see products under £15, £15 to £25, £25 to £50 and over £50.

Yes, 116 kits, routines, miniature sets and gift sets. See Gifts & Sets.

faq: What should I look for in a moisturiser for dry skin?
Richer textures that combine humectants with nourishing oils or butters. Hyaluronic acid, aloe vera, milk proteins, shea butter and almond oil all help skin hold on to moisture.
How often should I moisturise dry skin?
Morning and night, on clean, slightly damp skin. In the morning, finish with SPF.
Are natural moisturisers good for dry skin?
Plant-based creams from Vilvah and Deyga use oils, butters and milk proteins to cushion dry skin. Patch test first if your skin is sensitive.

kw.d: Deep-conditioning hair masks and treatments for dry, brittle hair: weekly care with natural oils and proteins.
faq: How often should I use a hair mask on dry hair?
Once or twice a week, after shampooing. Leave it on for 10 to 20 minutes, then rinse well.
Should I use a hair mask instead of conditioner?
Use both: conditioner after every wash, and a mask once a week for deeper care.
Can I use a hair mask on coloured hair?
Most natural masks are gentle enough for coloured hair. Check the product details before use.

kw.d: Nourishing hair oils for dry, frizzy and brittle hair, from coconut, castor and amla blends to lightweight serums.
faq: How do I use hair oil for dry hair?
Warm a few drops between your palms and massage into the scalp and lengths. Leave for at least an hour or overnight, then shampoo.
Can I use hair oil every day?
A pre-wash oil twice a week suits most dry hair. Use a few drops of a lightweight oil or serum on the ends daily for shine.
Which oils are best for dry hair?
Coconut, almond, argan and castor oils are popular choices; they coat the hair and help reduce breakage from dryness.

kw.d: Gentle, creamy face washes that cleanse without leaving dry skin tight, with milk, oat, honey and aloe.
faq: What kind of face wash is best for dry skin?
A gentle, non-foaming or low-foaming cleanser with soothing ingredients like milk, oat or aloe, free from harsh sulphates.
How often should I wash dry skin?
Once or twice a day. At night is most important, to remove sunscreen and the day’s build-up.
Can I use the same face wash morning and night?
Yes. Dry skin can also just rinse with water in the morning and cleanse properly at night.

kw.d: Clarifying face washes for oily and blemish-prone skin, with charcoal, neem, tea tree and clay.
faq: What should a face wash for oily skin do?
Remove excess oil and impurities without stripping the skin, so it does not over-produce oil afterwards.
How often should I wash oily skin?
Twice a day is enough. Washing more often can leave skin feeling tight and oilier later.
Is charcoal face wash good for oily skin?
Charcoal is popular for oily skin because it helps lift away oil and impurities from the surface.

kw.d: Natural anti-dandruff shampoos with neem, tea tree and herbal actives for a calm, flake-free-looking scalp.
faq: How often should I use an anti-dandruff shampoo?
Two to three times a week at first, then once or twice a week to keep flakes away.
How do I use dandruff shampoo for best results?
Massage into the scalp and leave for two to three minutes before rinsing, so the ingredients can work.
Can I use conditioner with dandruff shampoo?
Yes. Apply conditioner to the lengths only, keeping it off the scalp.

kw.d: Body lotions, creams and butters for dry skin, with goat milk, shea, cocoa and plant oils.
faq: When should I apply body lotion on dry skin?
Straight after a shower or bath, on slightly damp skin, to lock in moisture.
Lotion or body butter for very dry skin?
Lotions absorb faster for daily use. Body butters are richer and best for very dry areas like elbows, knees and feet.
Is goat milk lotion good for dry skin?
Goat milk is naturally rich in fats and proteins, which is why it is popular in lotions for dry skin.

kw.d: Lightweight hair serums and oils to smooth frizz and add shine without weighing hair down.
faq: How do I use hair serum for frizz?
Smooth one or two drops over damp or dry lengths and ends, avoiding the roots.
Hair serum or hair oil for frizzy hair?
Serums are lighter and best for daily styling; oils give deeper nourishment as a pre-wash treatment.
Can I use hair serum every day?
Yes, a small amount daily is fine for most hair types.

kw.d: Nourishing lip balms, butters and scrubs for dry, chapped lips, including Deyga’s cult beetroot lip balm.
faq: What is the best lip balm for dry lips?
Look for butters and oils such as shea, cocoa, almond and jojoba, without petroleum jelly or artificial fragrance.
How often should I apply lip balm?
Whenever lips feel dry, and always before bed. Use an SPF lip balm outdoors.
Should I exfoliate dry lips?
Gently, once or twice a week, with a lip scrub, then follow with balm.

kw.d: Alcohol-free toners and rose waters that refresh and hydrate dry skin before serum and moisturiser.
faq: Do I need a toner for dry skin?
A hydrating, alcohol-free toner adds a layer of moisture and helps serums and creams absorb.
How do I use toner?
After cleansing, pat onto skin with your hands or a cotton pad, then apply serum and moisturiser.
Is rose water good for dry skin?
Rose water is a gentle, refreshing toner that suits most skin types, including dry skin.

kw.d: Daily sunscreens and SPF from natural skincare brands, lightweight enough to wear under make-up.
faq: How much sunscreen should I use on my face?
About two finger-lengths for the face and neck, reapplied every two hours outdoors.
Do I need sunscreen in the UK?
Yes. UV reaches the skin all year, even on cloudy days, so daily SPF is a good habit.
Can I wear sunscreen under make-up?
Yes. Apply it as the last step of your skincare and let it settle for a minute before make-up.

kw.d: Natural shampoos from Vilvah and Deyga with rice water, goat milk, soy and herbs: free from harsh sulphates and parabens.
faq: What makes a shampoo natural?
Plant-based cleansing ingredients and botanical extracts, without harsh sulphates, parabens or synthetic colours.
Will a natural shampoo lather less?
Often a little less, because it uses gentler cleansers. It still cleans well; use a second wash if needed.
Are Vilvah and Deyga shampoos sold in the UK?
Yes. Swansura is an official UK partner of both brands and ships from the UK.

kw.d: Rich body butters for very dry skin, with shea, cocoa and nourishing oils.
faq: How do I use body butter?
Warm a small amount between your hands and massage into slightly damp skin after a shower.
Body butter or lotion?
Body butter is richer and best for very dry skin or night-time; lotion is lighter for everyday use.
Can I use body butter on my face?
Body butters are made for the body. Use a face moisturiser for your face.

kw.d: Hair growth oils with traditional ingredients like amla, bhringraj, onion and castor, to nourish the scalp and roots.
faq: How do I use hair growth oil?
Massage a small amount into the scalp with your fingertips, leave for at least an hour or overnight, then shampoo.
How often should I oil my scalp?
Two or three times a week is a common routine.
When will I see results?
Hair grows slowly, so give any routine at least two to three months of regular use.

kw.d: Clay, charcoal and mud masks that absorb excess oil and leave skin feeling clean and refreshed.
faq: How often should I use a face mask for oily skin?
Once or twice a week, on clean skin.
How long should I leave a clay mask on?
Until it is almost dry, usually 10 to 15 minutes; don’t let it crack completely.
Do I need to moisturise after a clay mask?
Yes. Follow with a light moisturiser to keep skin balanced.

kw.d: Natural lip scrubs with sugar and plant oils to buff away dry, flaky skin before balm.
faq: How often should I use a lip scrub?
Once or twice a week. More often can irritate the lips.
How do I use a lip scrub?
Massage a small amount onto damp lips in circles for 20 to 30 seconds, wipe or rinse off, then apply lip balm.
Can I use a lip scrub before lipstick?
Yes. Scrub, then balm, and wait a few minutes before lipstick for a smoother finish.

kw.d: Night creams, elixirs and overnight masks that nourish skin while you sleep.
faq: Do I need a separate night cream?
Night creams are usually richer than day creams and skip SPF, so they suit the slower overnight routine.
When should I apply night cream?
As the last step of your evening routine, after cleansing, toner and serum.
Can I use night cream during the day?
It is best at night; in the day, use a moisturiser with SPF or follow with sunscreen.

kw.d: Gentle, strengthening shampoos with rice water, onion and herbal extracts, for hair that is prone to breakage and shedding.
faq: Can a shampoo stop hair loss?
No shampoo can stop hair loss on its own, but a gentle, strengthening shampoo helps reduce breakage from washing and styling.
How often should I wash thinning hair?
Two to three times a week with a mild shampoo suits most people.
What else helps with hair fall?
A scalp oil routine, gentle brushing and a balanced diet. See a GP or trichologist if hair loss is sudden.

journal.t: Deyga or Vilvah: which natural brand suits your skin?
journal.d: Farm-grown botanicals or goat milk care? A simple guide to both official partner brands.
journal.mt: Deyga or Vilvah? Natural Skincare UK Guide | Swansura
journal.md: Deyga or Vilvah? How the two Indian natural skincare brands differ, what to try first, and how to build a simple routine. Both ship from the UK.
journal.body:
If you are looking for natural skincare in the UK with roots in Indian beauty traditions, two names come up again and again: Deyga and Vilvah. Both are Indian brands, both work with plant-based and kitchen-cupboard ingredients, and Swansura is an official UK partner of both, so every product is genuine and ships from the UK. They are not the same, though. Here is how to tell which one suits your skin, and where to start.

The short answer

Choose Vilvah if you like creamy, comforting textures built around goat milk, oat milk and gentle botanicals. Choose Deyga if you prefer farm-grown herbs, clays, charcoal and fruit actives with a fresher feel. Many people end up using both: a Vilvah cleanser or serum in the morning and a Deyga treat, such as a lip balm or face pack, alongside it.

Vilvah: goat milk and botanical care

Vilvah is known for milk-based formulas for face, hair and body. The best place to start is Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum, a lightweight milk serum with natural milk proteins that sinks in quickly and leaves skin feeling soft rather than greasy. It is the product people search for most: "Vilvah Milk Drops" is one of the brand's top searches in the UK.

For hair, the Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo pairs goat milk with pea protein and jasmine. It is pH-balanced and free from artificial colours and fragrances, so it suits frequent washing, and it is a good fit for dry or frizzy hair. If you want the full ritual, the Goat Milk Hair Kit puts the shampoo with its partners in one box.

For the body, Vilvah Milk Body Lotion uses oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane in a quick-absorbing, vegan formula that is gentle enough for the whole family. Prefer a no-scent wash? The Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is the calmest place to begin. See the whole range on our goat milk edit.

Deyga: farm-grown botanicals

Deyga makes natural skin, hair and body care with plant-based ingredients, many grown on its own farm in India. Its cult favourite is the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: beetroot extract and natural butters give a soft, sheer tint, and the 10 g tin fits any pocket. "Deyga lip balm" is one of the brand's most searched products, and it makes an easy first try at under £11.

For oilier or combination skin, the Deyga Charcoal Face Wash uses activated charcoal for a deep, refreshing cleanse without a tight finish. For glow, the Deyga Rose Glow Serum is a light rose and saffron oil serum that leaves skin looking radiant. On wash day, Deyga Rice Water Shampoo is a gentle, sulfate-free everyday cleanser.

Which is better for your skin type?

Dry or sensitive skin

Lean towards Vilvah. Milk textures, fragrance-free options and the oat milk body lotion are made for comfort. Add a Deyga body butter for dry skin, such as the Chocolate Body Butter, for extra richness on elbows and legs.

Oily or combination skin

Start with Deyga's charcoal face wash and a lightweight serum, then use a Vilvah milk product only where skin feels dry. Our face wash for oily skin page compares the options side by side.

Dull-looking skin

Try one serum from each brand on alternate days: Vilvah Milk Drops for hydration and Deyga Rose Glow for radiance. Keep everything else simple.

A simple routine using both brands

  1. Cleanse: Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (oilier skin) or Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (drier skin).
  2. Treat: Vilvah Milk Drops in the morning, Deyga Rose Glow in the evening.
  3. Lips and body: Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm through the day and Vilvah Milk Body Lotion after showering.

Patch test anything new and introduce one product at a time. Ready-made pairings with 5% off are on our routines page.

Why buy Deyga and Vilvah from Swansura?

We are an official UK partner of both brands, so there are no grey imports and no long waits from abroad: orders are dispatched from the UK, usually within 1–2 working days, with free UK delivery over £40. Explore the full natural skincare edit, or go straight to all Deyga and all Vilvah products.

journal.t: How to layer oud with body butter so it lasts all day
journal.d: Why fragrance lasts longer on moisturised skin, and three pairings to try.
journal.mt: How to Layer Oud Perfume with Body Butter | Swansura UK
journal.md: Make oud perfume last longer by layering it over body butter. Why it works, how to apply it and three skin + scent pairings to try, shipped from the UK.
journal.body:
Oud is one of the richest notes in perfumery: smoky, resinous and warm. Yet even a great oud perfume can fade sooner than you expect on dry skin. The fix is simple and costs very little: layer it over a body butter. Here is why it works, how to do it, and three pairings from our shelves to try.

Why fragrance lasts longer on moisturised skin

Perfume oils evaporate fastest from dry skin. A thin layer of butter or lotion gives the fragrance something to cling to, so it tends to unfold more slowly and stay closer to you for longer. Rich butters with cocoa, shea or almond oil work especially well under warm notes such as oud, amber and vanilla. If your skin runs dry, a body butter for dry skin does two jobs at once.

How to layer, step by step

  1. Shower first. Pat skin almost dry; slightly damp skin takes butter more evenly.
  2. Warm a little butter between your palms and press it into pulse points: wrists, inner elbows, the base of the neck and behind the knees.
  3. Wait a minute so the butter settles.
  4. Spray once or twice from about 15 cm onto the same spots. Don't rub your wrists together; let it dry.
  5. Top up the butter, not the perfume, later in the day if skin feels dry. The scent often comes back with it.

Three skin + scent pairings to try

1. Sweet and golden: Chocolate Body Butter + Amber Oud Gold

The Deyga Chocolate Body Butter is made with cocoa and nourishing oils and has a light chocolate scent. Under Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition, with its melon, pineapple, vanilla and musk, it reads as a soft gourmand. For more intensity, try the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait. "Chocolate body butter" and "Al Haramain Amber Oud" are both popular UK searches, and this is the pairing that shows why.

2. Floral and warm: Rose & Geranium Body Butter + Amber Oud Ruby

The Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter carries rose and geranium essential oils. Layer it under Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition, which opens with saffron and bitter almond over jasmine, cedarwood, ambergris and musk, and the florals meet in the middle. If you love rose with oud, Montale Aoud Damascus is another lovely match.

3. Clean and smoky: a light lotion + Gucci Intense Oud

Not every pairing needs a scented base. A light, quick-absorbing lotion such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion lets a dark scent like Gucci Intense Oud (black pepper, incense, woods, leather and an oud accord) lead the way, while still giving it something to hold on to. Want a luxury option? Try Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter.

Which base suits your skin?

If your skin is very dry, a rich butter such as Deyga's cocoa or rose formulas gives the most staying power. If you prefer something lighter in warm weather, a lotion like Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion absorbs faster and still helps the fragrance last. On sensitive days, keep the base unscented and let the perfume do the talking.

A few tips for oud

  • Less is more. Oud projects well; one or two sprays over butter usually lasts.
  • Spray clothes lightly, not silk, to keep a soft trail.
  • Match the mood. Sweet butters suit amber ouds, floral butters suit rose ouds, and neutral lotions suit smoky ouds.

Browse every oud perfume we stock, the full oud scent family, or our body butter edit. Each pairing above also makes a thoughtful gift, and orders over £40 ship free across the UK.
faq: Does body butter make perfume last longer?
Fragrance usually lasts longer on moisturised skin because the oils evaporate more slowly. Apply a thin layer of butter to pulse points, then spray over it.
Should the body butter be scented or unscented?
Either works. Choose a scent that shares notes with your perfume, such as chocolate under amber and vanilla or rose under a rose oud, or use a light, neutral lotion under smoky ouds.
Which oud perfume is best for layering?
Warm, sweet ouds such as Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold and Ruby Editions layer easily over body butter. Smoky ouds like Gucci Intense Oud suit a neutral lotion.

journal.t: Extrait vs eau de parfum: what the label means
journal.d: Concentration, longevity and how close a scent sits to the skin.
journal.mt: Extrait vs Eau de Parfum vs EDT: What It Means | Swansura
journal.md: Extrait de parfum, eau de parfum or eau de toilette? What the label means for strength, longevity and price, with examples you can shop in the UK.
kw: Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition
journal.body:
Extrait de parfum, eau de parfum, eau de toilette: the words on the bottle tell you how concentrated the fragrance is. That affects how long it lasts, how far it travels and, often, the price. Here is what each label means and how to choose.

The labels, from strongest to lightest

Extrait de parfum (also "parfum")

The most concentrated form, typically around 20–40% perfume oil. Extraits sit close to the skin, develop slowly and can last from morning to evening. Italian house Tiziana Terenzi is known for them: Kaff Extrait de Parfum opens with bergamot, juniper and white iris before lavender, magnolia and leather settle into amber, musk and woods. Tiziana Terenzi Kirke, one of the house's most searched perfumes in the UK, is a fruity extrait, and Gold Rose Oudh brings rose and oud together.

Eau de parfum (EDP)

Usually around 15–20% perfume oil, and the most popular strength today. An EDP has good projection and wears for several hours. Good examples: Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition and Calvin Klein Eternity Eau de Parfum.

Eau de toilette (EDT)

Lighter, typically around 5–15%, with a bright opening that suits daytime and warm weather. Try Calvin Klein Eternity for Men Eau de Toilette or Davidoff Champion.

These ranges are typical, not fixed rules. Every house sets its own formula, which is why one brand's EDP can outlast another's extrait.

Same name, different strength

Many perfumes come in more than one concentration, and they don't always smell identical. Al Haramain's Amber Oud Gold Edition eau de parfum and the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait share the same fruity amber notes, but the extrait feels richer and closer to the skin. Calvin Klein's Eternity comes as an EDT, an EDP and a parfum miniature, which is an easy way to compare.

Which should you choose?

  • For all-day wear and evenings: an extrait, or an EDP layered over body butter.
  • For the office and everyday: an EDP, with one or two sprays.
  • For hot weather or the gym bag: an EDT, which you can reapply freely.
  • For gifting: an EDP is the safe choice; a travel-size mini lets someone try a new strength first.

Other words you might see on the label

  • Intense, Extreme or Elixir: a richer version of an existing scent. It is often closer to an extrait in feel, but there is no fixed rule, so check the notes.
  • Cologne or eau de cologne: the lightest style, usually fresh and citrusy, made for a quick lift.
  • ml: the bottle size. A 10 ml miniature is a low-cost way to test a scent on your own skin before buying 100 ml.

How to make any concentration last longer

Whatever the label says, skin matters. Fragrance tends to last longer on moisturised skin, so apply a little body lotion or butter to pulse points first, then spray. Keep bottles out of sunlight and heat, and avoid rubbing your wrists together. Our guide to layering oud with body butter walks through it step by step, and the body lotion for dry skin edit has easy bases to try.

Is extrait worth the price?

Per spray, often yes: you use less, and it lasts longer. But "stronger" doesn't mean "better". Choose the scent first and the concentration second. faq: What is the difference between extrait de parfum and eau de parfum?
Extrait de parfum has a higher concentration of perfume oil (typically around 20–40%) than eau de parfum (around 15–20%), so it usually lasts longer and sits closer to the skin.
Is eau de parfum stronger than eau de toilette?
Usually, yes. Eau de parfum typically contains more perfume oil than eau de toilette, so it lasts longer, while an EDT feels lighter and brighter.
Do extrait and EDP versions smell the same?
Not always. Houses often adjust the formula, so an extrait can feel richer or warmer than the eau de parfum with the same name.
